subject: Performance SLO follow-up: context window, tokens, and latency impact

Subject: Performance SLO follow-up: context window, tokens, and latency impact

Hi Samir --

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

What I heard from FinCo:
- Primary product: transaction summarization + policy classification in the underwriting flow.
- Typical input: ~3-4k tokens, peaks up to ~8k tokens for long transcripts.
- Output: ~300-600 tokens (most cases ~512).
- Streaming required (clients expect immediate partial results while generation continues).
- Target concurrency: ~50 concurrent users hitting the service during peak.
- Target throughput: ~80-120 req/s across the fleet.
- Latency goal: p95 end-to-end <= 400ms if possible; p99 SLA to be discussed.

Open questions we flagged on the call:
1) Confirm average vs peak token numbers (you mentioned 3-4k typical, 8k peak).
2) Which percentiles (p95/p99) are most important for the user experience?
3) Any hard regulatory requirements for data residency or KMS?

Attached is a short SLO/spec sheet that outlines the metrics we typically benchmark against (SLO_spec_sheet.pdf). Rishi from our SE team (cc'd) will outline a recommended test matrix and estimated latency/throughput trade-offs for different context window sizes and model variants.

Proposed next steps:
- Rishi to share a preliminary latency estimate and recommended test config (today).
- Schedule a 60-min benchmark alignment session week of 4/18 to finalize test dataset and ramp plan.
- Send us a sample of representative prompts (anonymized) and a short traffic profile (req/s by minute) so we can size the test.

If any of the bullets above are inaccurate, please let me know. Otherwise, can you confirm the typical/peak token counts and whether 4/19 or 4/20 at 10am PT works for the benchmark sync?

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: context window, tokens, and latency impact

Hi Samir / Marissa --

Following up with technical notes based on the targets you shared. High level: context window (input + output tokens) is the dominant factor for generative latency; beyond a few thousand tokens the per-token generation time and KV cache size materially increase memory and compute. A few concrete points and mitigations: 

Quick estimates (ballpark) -- p95 generation-only latency (no network/transport):
- 4k input + 512 output: ~220-380ms on a compact 7B-class model with optimized kernels (quantized FP16/INT8 path).
- 8k input + 512 output (peak): ~550-900ms depending on model and quantization.

What affects those numbers:
- Model family & size: larger models => higher per-token time.
- Quantization & kernel selection: INT8/4-bit quant gives ~1.5-2x improvement over FP16 in many cases.
- Batching: improves throughput but increases tail latency if not configured carefully.
- Streaming (chunked output): improves perceived latency (first byte) significantly -- we typically see 40-60% reduction in time-to-first-token using streaming with prefix caching.

Recommended test config for the benchmark run:
- Model: redwood-7b-8k (quantized INT8), fallback to 13B if quality needed.
- Batch sizing: start with batch_size=16 for latency-focused tests, ramp to 32/64 for throughput tests.
- Concurrency: run 50 concurrent virtual users during peak tests; also run a 200-concurrency soak for degradation characteristics.
- Streaming: enable server-side streaming with chunk size ~64 tokens to measure perceived latency.

Attachments: I attached a short CSV with latency estimates across token ranges (latency-estimates.csv). It includes our measured p50/p95/p99 numbers from recent benchmarks on similar workloads. 

Notes on trade-offs to discuss on the call:
- If p95 <= 400ms is a hard requirement even for 8k inputs, we should explore: sharding the request (front-end trim + incremental context), stronger quantization, or a smaller model ensemble for fast first-pass results + async refinement for final output.
- Cost -> throughput trade: aggressive batching + larger GPUs lower $/token but increase tail latency.

Happy to walk through the CSV on 4/19 and run an initial 48-hour pilot next week if FinCo can provide anonymized sample prompts.

Cheers,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
